**Internal Handoff Brief: Y-Office Tower Engineering Project**

---

### 1. Project Overview

The Y-Office Tower project for client AE Prime in New Cairo, Egypt, involves the comprehensive engineering design for a high-rise office building spanning a total built-up area of 32,025 m², including 27 office floors and multiple basement levels. The core objective is to deliver a complete LOD-350 Revit model across all disciplines, alongside detailed structural analysis, advanced power systems including MV intake and standby generation, and specialized gas suppression systems. The project is slated for completion by August 1, 2026.

### 2. Discipline Tasks

**Architect:**
The Architectural team is responsible for developing all design documentation, starting with Schematic Architecture Drawings and progressing to detailed Architecture Plans, Elevations, Sections, and various detail drawings (Stair, Wet Areas, Wall Sections). They will also produce 3D visualizations (Shots, Views, Perspectives), a comprehensive Bill of Quantity, and the foundational Architectural Revit Model (LOD 350). Their initial work is contingent on receiving the General Report 1 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0001).

**Structural Engineer:**
The Structural team will undertake the complete structural design and analysis, beginning with Schematic Structural Drawings. This includes detailed Structural Calculation Reports, ETABS and SAFE models, and specific design calculations for columns, shear walls, and retaining walls. Key deliverables include Structural Plans, Columns & Axis Drawings, General Notes and Details, Reinforcement Drawings for cores and slabs, and a comprehensive Structural Revit Model (LOD 350). Inputs required are the Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001) and General Report 1 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0001).

**HVAC Engineer:**
The HVAC team is tasked with designing the building's heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems. This involves producing Schematic HVAC Drawings, various calculation reports (Heat Load, Exhaust, Pressurization, Ventilation, Smoke Evacuation), and detailed drawings for ductwork, pipework, riser diagrams, schematics, and system plans. They will also deliver a Bill of Quantity and the HVAC Revit Model. Their work depends on the Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001) and General Report 2 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0002).

**Plumbing Engineer:**
The Plumbing team will design all water supply and drainage systems. Their deliverables include Schematic Plumbing Drawings, a Plumbing Calculation Report, and detailed layouts for water supply and drainage systems. They are also responsible for drawings of the water supply pump room and tanks, plumbing schematics, toilet details, general details, and a Bill of Quantity, culminating in the Plumbing Revit Model. Key inputs are the Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001) and General Report 2 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0002).

**Fire Fighting Engineer:**
The Fire Fighting team will develop the fire protection and suppression systems. This includes Schematic Fire Fighting Drawings, specific calculation reports for CO2/FM-200 suppression in critical rooms (electrical, low current, generator, transformer), and a Fire Sprinkler Report. They will produce Fire Fighting System Layouts, Schematics, General Details, and drawings for the pump room and tanks, along with a Bill of Quantity and the Fire Fighting Revit Model. This discipline has several dependencies: Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001), Electrical Drawing General Notes (PRJ.23026-EL-DGN-5001), Single Line Diagram Drawings (PRJ.23026-EL-SLD-5001), General Report 2 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0002), HVAC Duct Work System Drawings (PRJ.23026-HV-DKS-3001), and the Plumbing Calculation Report (PRJ.23026-PL-CAL-7001).

**Low Current Engineer:**
The Low Current team is responsible for designing all low current systems, starting with Schematic Low Current Drawings. This encompasses detailed system drawings for Fire Alarm, CCTV, Access Control, Public Address, and Structured Cabling. They will also provide Riser Diagrams, Schematics, a Legend, a Bill of Quantity, and various Low Current Revit Models (overall, detailed, and schematic). Their work relies on Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001), Fire Fighting System Layout Drawings (PRJ.23026-FF-FFS-4001), General Report 2 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0002), and HVAC Duct Work System Drawings (PRJ.23026-HV-DKS-3001).

**Electrical Engineer:**
The Electrical team will design the entire electrical power distribution and lighting systems. Deliverables include Schematic Electrical Drawings, various calculation reports (LUX, Electrical Load, Cable Tray, Earthing, Lighting, Transformer/MV Sizing), Electrical Drawing General Notes, Schematics, Single Line Diagrams, Panelboard Schedules, Lighting System Layouts (general and emergency), Small Power System, Mechanical Power System, and Cable Routing drawings, along with a Bill of Quantity and the Electrical Revit Model. Key inputs are Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001), General Report 2 (PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0002), Heat Load Calculation Report (PRJ.23026-HV-CAL-3001), and Plumbing Calculation Report (PRJ.23026-PL-CAL-7001).

### 3. Risk Flags & Engineering Implications

*   **Medium Voltage (MV) Intake:** The design must account for a 13.8 kV MV intake. This necessitates detailed transformer sizing, selection of MV switchgear/Ring Main Units (RMU), and precise MV cable sizing. The Electrical team must ensure the inclusion of the specific Transformer / MV Sizing Calculation (EL-CAL-5006) as a key deliverable.

*   **Standby Power Required:** Essential and life-safety loads must be segregated onto a dedicated emergency/standby board. The Electrical team is responsible for confirming the appropriate sizing of the standby diesel generator and UPS systems to meet these critical loads, adhering to relevant standards such as ISO 8528 and EN 1838 for emergency lighting.

*   **High-Rise Implications:** The high-rise nature of the Y-Office Tower introduces several design complexities. The Electrical team must address rising busway sizing and voltage drop calculations over vertical runs. Lightning protection design, in accordance with IEC 62305, is also critical. For HVAC, stair pressurization systems are required, and Plumbing must design for pumped water zones to ensure adequate pressure at higher levels.

*   **Deep Basement Implications:** The multiple deep basement levels require specific engineering considerations. The Structural team must prioritize the Retaining Walls Design Calculations (ST-CAL-9003). Plumbing will need to design robust sump and drainage pump systems for effective water management. The HVAC team is responsible for designing the garage CO ventilation system to ensure air quality in these enclosed spaces.

### 4. Key Dates

*   **2026-03-14:** Initial Schematic Drawings due for Architecture, Structural, HVAC, Plumbing, Fire Fighting, Low Current, and Electrical disciplines.
*   **2026-03-28:** Architectural 3D Shots, Views, Perspectives, and Presentation due. Structural Soil Borings due.
*   **2026-04-11:** Architecture Plans Drawings (PRJ.23026-AR-ARP-1001) due – a critical input for multiple disciplines.
*   **2026-04-25:** Structural ETABS and SAFE Models due.
*   **2026-05-09:** Architectural and Structural Revit Models (LOD 350) due. HVAC Heat Load Calculation Report due.
*   **2026-05-23:** HVAC, Plumbing, Fire Fighting, Low Current, and Electrical Revit Models due.
*   **2026-05-30:** Electrical Transformer / MV Sizing Calculation (EL-CAL-5006) due.
*   **2026-06-06:** Electrical Single Line Diagram (PRJ.23026-EL-SLD-5001) due.
*   **2026-06-27:** All Bills of Quantity (BOQ) due across all disciplines.
*   **2026-07-04:** Structural Comment Response Sheets due.
*   **2026-08-01:** Project End Date.

## 1. Introduction

### 1.1 Document Identification

### 1.2 Project Identification

*   **Project Name:** Y-Office Tower
*   **Client:** AE Prime
*   **Location:** New Cairo, Egypt
*   **Project End Date:** 2026-08-01

### 1.3 Purpose of this Plan

The Project Execution Plan (PEP) outlines the comprehensive strategy and methodology for managing, executing, and controlling the Y-Office Tower project. This document specifically details the plan for executing the project phases corresponding to Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) levels 0 through 2, encompassing overall project management, conceptual design, and schematic design stages. It serves as a foundational reference for all project participants, ensuring alignment with project objectives, client requirements, and established engineering standards.

## 2. Project Overview

### 2.1 Project Description

The Y-Office Tower project involves the design and engineering of a modern office tower located in New Cairo, Egypt. The project encompasses architectural, structural, and comprehensive Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing (MEP) design, including HVAC, Plumbing, Fire Fighting, Low Current, and Electrical systems.

### 2.2 Key Project Characteristics

*   **Building Type:** High-rise Office Tower
*   **Basement:** Deep Basement
*   **Power Supply:** Medium Voltage Intake, Standby Power Required
*   **Process Data:** Not applicable (building project, no specific process equipment/fluids)

### 2.3 Project Objectives

The primary objectives of the Y-Office Tower project are to:
*   Deliver a complete and high-quality engineering design package for the Y-Office Tower within the agreed schedule and budget.
*   Ensure all designs comply with local regulations, international standards, and client specifications.
*   Effectively manage project risks, particularly those associated with high-rise construction, deep basements, and complex power systems.
*   Foster clear communication and collaboration among all project stakeholders.

## 3. Project Scope (WBS 0-2)

This Project Execution Plan focuses on the initial and foundational phases of the project, as defined by WBS 0, 1, and 2.

### 3.1 Overall Project Management (WBS 0)

WBS 0 covers the overarching project management and administrative activities necessary to ensure the successful execution of the project. This includes:
*   **Project Planning:** Development and maintenance of project plans, including this PEP, the Project Schedule, and other subsidiary management plans.
*   **Project Integration:** Coordinating all project elements and ensuring seamless integration across disciplines.
*   **Stakeholder Management:** Identifying, analyzing, and engaging with all project stakeholders.
*   **Communication Management:** Establishing clear communication channels and protocols.
*   **Risk Management:** Proactive identification, assessment, and mitigation of project risks.
*   **Quality Management:** Defining and implementing quality assurance and control processes.
*   **Document Control:** Managing all project documentation, including the Document Register.

### 3.2 Engineering Design & Deliverables (WBS 1 & 2)

WBS 1 encompasses the overall engineering design phase, while WBS 2 breaks down the design into specific disciplines and their initial deliverables. This project is heavily focused on the design phase, covering:

*   **Architectural Design:** Conceptual and schematic architectural layouts, elevations, sections, and 3D visualizations.
*   **Structural Design:** Conceptual and schematic structural layouts, including preliminary analysis and design considerations for the high-rise and deep basement.
*   **MEP Design (General):** Conceptual and schematic design for all Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing systems.
    *   **HVAC Design:** Schematic HVAC system layouts, preliminary heat load calculations.
    *   **Plumbing Design:** Schematic plumbing system layouts, preliminary calculations.
    *   **Fire Fighting Design:** Schematic fire fighting system layouts, preliminary reports.
    *   **Low Current Design:** Schematic low current system layouts (Fire Alarm, CCTV, Access Control, Public Address, Structured Cabling).
    *   **Electrical Design:** Schematic electrical layouts, preliminary load calculations, single line diagrams.

A detailed list of key deliverables for these WBS levels is provided in Appendix A.

## 4. Project Organization and Responsibilities

The project organization is structured to ensure clear lines of authority, effective communication, and efficient execution.

### 4.1 Project Management Team

The Project Management (PM) team is responsible for the overall planning, execution, monitoring, control, and closeout of the project.
*   **Project Manager (PM):** Overall responsibility for project success, client liaison, budget, schedule, risk, and quality.

### 4.2 Engineering Discipline Leads

Each engineering discipline is led by a dedicated engineer responsible for their respective scope of work, technical quality, and timely delivery of documentation.
*   **Architect:** Responsible for architectural design, aesthetics, space planning, and compliance with building codes.
*   **Structural Engineer:** Responsible for the structural integrity, stability, and safety of the building, including foundation and superstructure design.
*   **HVAC Engineer:** Responsible for heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system design.
*   **Plumbing Engineer:** Responsible for water supply, drainage, and sanitary system design.
*   **Fire Fighting Engineer:** Responsible for fire detection, suppression, and life safety system design.
*   **Low Current Engineer:** Responsible for telecommunications, security, and other low voltage systems.
*   **Electrical Engineer:** Responsible for power distribution, lighting, and earthing system design.

### 6.2 Schedule Control

### 6.4 Quality Management

### 6.5 Risk Management

A comprehensive Risk Management Plan will be implemented to address identified project risks.
*   **High-Rise Construction:** Specific design considerations for wind loads, seismic activity, vertical transportation, and fire safety will be integrated.
*   **Deep Basement:** Geotechnical investigations, dewatering strategies, and structural design for retaining walls will be critical.
*   **Medium Voltage Intake & Standby Power:** Detailed electrical design will address power supply reliability, redundancy, and safety requirements.

## 4.0 MEP Concept Design Philosophy

The MEP concept design for the Y-Office Tower is driven by principles of efficiency, sustainability, reliability, safety, and maintainability. The design aims to provide a comfortable, productive, and secure environment for occupants while minimizing operational costs and environmental impact.

This report builds upon the foundational architectural and structural concepts established in PRJ.23026-GE-REP-0001 (Architectural and Structural Concept Design Report), ensuring seamless integration and coordination across all disciplines.

## 5.0 Discipline-Specific Concept Design

### 5.1 Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC)

The HVAC concept for the high-rise Y-Office Tower will focus on providing optimal thermal comfort and indoor air quality, considering the New Cairo climate.

*   **System Type**: A central plant approach with chilled water distribution is envisioned, potentially supplemented by VRF (Variable Refrigerant Flow) systems for specific zones or tenant flexibility.
*   **Zoning**: Due to the high-rise nature, the building will be divided into multiple HVAC zones to allow for independent control and energy optimization based on occupancy and solar exposure.
*   **Ventilation**: Dedicated outdoor air systems (DOAS) will be considered to ensure adequate fresh air supply. Exhaust systems will be designed for wet areas, kitchens, and specialized spaces.
*   **Smoke Management**: A critical aspect for a high-rise, the design will incorporate robust smoke extraction and pressurization systems for stairwells and lift shafts, in compliance with international and local fire codes.
*   **Energy Efficiency**: High-efficiency chillers, pumps, fans, and heat recovery systems will be evaluated to reduce energy consumption.

### 5.2 Plumbing and Drainage

The plumbing and drainage systems will be designed to provide reliable water supply and efficient waste removal throughout the high-rise structure and deep basement.

*   **Water Supply**: A multi-zone pressurized water supply system will be implemented to manage the high static pressures associated with a high-rise building. This will include potable water, and potentially non-potable water for irrigation or toilet flushing (greywater recycling).
*   **Hot Water**: Centralized or localized hot water generation systems will be considered based on demand profiles.
*   **Drainage**: Separate sanitary and storm drainage systems will be designed. The deep basement will require dedicated sump pump systems for groundwater and potential wastewater removal.
*   **Fixtures**: Water-efficient fixtures will be specified to minimize water consumption.

### 5.3 Fire Fighting Systems

Fire fighting systems are paramount for the safety of a high-rise office tower and will be designed to meet stringent international and local fire codes.

*   **Active Fire Protection**:
    *   **Sprinkler System**: A fully automatic sprinkler system will be designed for comprehensive coverage throughout the building.
    *   **Standpipe System**: Wet standpipe systems with fire hose reels will be strategically located on all floors.
    *   **Fire Pumps & Tanks**: Dedicated fire pumps and water storage tanks will be sized to meet the required flow and pressure demands.
*   **Special Hazard Suppression**: Given the "medium_voltage_intake" and "standby_power_required" risk flags, specialized clean agent (e.g., FM-200) or CO2 suppression systems will be incorporated for critical areas such as transformer rooms, generator rooms, and main electrical/low current rooms.
*   **Passive Fire Protection**: Coordination with architectural and structural teams for fire-rated compartments, doors, and shaft enclosures.

### 5.4 Electrical Systems

The electrical concept design will ensure a reliable, safe, and efficient power supply for the entire Y-Office Tower, addressing the specific risk flags.

*   **Medium Voltage (MV) Intake**: The design will include a dedicated MV substation, switchgear, and transformers to step down the incoming medium voltage supply to the building's low voltage distribution. Redundancy will be explored.
*   **Low Voltage (LV) Distribution**: A robust LV distribution network will be designed, including main distribution boards (MDBs), sub-distribution boards (SDBs), and panelboards to serve all building loads.
*   **Standby Power**: A comprehensive standby power system will be integrated, comprising:
    *   **Generators**: Sized to support critical and essential loads during utility power outages.
    *   **Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS)**: For seamless transition between utility and generator power.
    *   **Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)**: For critical IT and safety systems requiring uninterrupted power.
*   **Lighting**: Energy-efficient LED lighting systems will be specified for general, task, and emergency lighting. LUX calculations will ensure adequate illumination levels.
*   **Small Power**: Sufficient power outlets will be provided for office equipment and tenant fit-out.
*   **Mechanical Power**: Dedicated power circuits for all HVAC, plumbing, and fire fighting equipment.
*   **Earthing & Lightning Protection**: A comprehensive earthing system and lightning protection system will be designed to protect the building and its occupants from electrical faults and lightning strikes.

### 5.5 Low Current Systems

The low current systems will provide essential communication, security, and life safety infrastructure for the modern office tower.

*   **Fire Alarm System (FAS)**: An addressable fire alarm system with smoke detectors, heat detectors, manual call points, and alarm notification devices will be designed in conjunction with the fire fighting systems.
*   **CCTV System**: A comprehensive CCTV surveillance system will be planned for security monitoring of common areas, entrances, and the perimeter.
*   **Access Control System**: An access control system will manage entry and exit points, enhancing building security.
*   **Public Address (PA) System**: A PA system will be integrated for announcements and emergency broadcasts.
*   **Structured Cabling System**: A robust structured cabling infrastructure (data and voice) will be designed to support the office tower's communication needs.
*   **Building Management System (BMS)**: A BMS will be considered for centralized monitoring and control of key MEP systems, optimizing energy usage and operational efficiency.
